ledger.note: 1531: the Nupe Kingdom. The page heads the kingdom "(1531-1835)" and says it "was established in the middle of the 15th century" between the Niger and Kaduna rivers; the early history relies mostly on oral legends.

ledger.note: 1835: the Nupe Kingdom becomes the Nupe Emirate under Gwandu. "After his [Ma'azu's] death the Nupe Kingdom came under the Gwandu Emirate during wars of succession"; Masaba, son of the Fulani leader Mallam Dendo, took power in 1841. The Sokoto dossier dates the fall c. 1808.

ledger.note: 1835: the Nupe Kingdom ends; the Nupe Emirate (1835-1901) is the Sokoto emirate of Bida, which "British [Niger Company] troops finally took ... and established a puppet ruler" in 1897.

wars.outcome: The Fulani gained power across Northern Nigeria in Ma'azu's time and Nupe came under Gwandu after his death in 1818; the page dates the emirate to 1835.
wars.note: The Sokoto dossier has the kingdom fall to Sokoto forces c. 1808 (Mallam Dendo installed as emir of Bida).

certainty.note: No frontier on the page; the kingdom is a river-basin core.

notes:
Nupe Kingdom, additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Page: Nupe Kingdom (1 page; thin).

Dates: the page's headings (1531-1835) against "the middle of the 15th century" in the text; the Fulani takeover is c. 1808 in the Sokoto dossier (Mallam Dendo as emir of Bida) and after 1818 on this page; the end is the page's 1835. The page has no infobox data, no founder (Tsoede), no capital (Gbara/Raba), no area and no account of expansion or of Oyo relations; the shape is a disc at Bida. The Nupe Emirate 1835-1901 belongs to the Sokoto Caliphate.
